title: Midnight clustered anomaly log - Jiwoo
content:
Context:
- Late-night sampling run on prod-mirror (smallish seed). Wanted to re-check recent fallback routing change (rollout 2024-11-10).
- Observed cluster of low-confidence, truncated responses across a narrow set of prompts. Pattern persisted across 3 hosts (gpu-12a, gpu-12b, gpu-14).

Top-line observation:
- ~18/120 sampled calls returned outputs that abruptly ended with partial sentence and increased repetition. Latency spiked slightly (~+40ms median). Token counts lower than expected.

Ad-hoc rubric (quick, 0-3):
- 0 = fine (no semantic drift, reply coherent)
- 1 = minor oddity (awkward phrasing, brief halluc)
- 2 = degraded (sentence cut, repetition, small factual error)
- 3 = fail (nonsensical, abrupt truncation, broken JSON/structure)

Scoring summary (manual quick pass, n=30 representative):
- 0: 9
- 1: 7
- 2: 10
- 3: 4  
(=> ~14/30 >=2 - higher than baseline from 2024-11-01 snapshot where >=2 was ~6/30)

Representative samples (prompt -> model output; edited for brevity):
1) Prompt: "Summarize policy for data retention in <company>"
   Output: "Retention policy: data stored for up to 90 days. For compliance, export and then..." (cuts mid-sentence) [score 3]

2) Prompt: "Write python snippet to parse ISO8601 and return epoch"
   Output: "def parse_iso(s):
    # naive parse
    return int(datetime.fromisoformat(s).timestamp())
    
    # TODO: handle timezone -" (ends, repeated indent) [score 2]

3) Prompt: "List risks of open endpoints"
   Output: "- unauthorized access
- data exfiltration
- rate limits
- unauthorized access
" (repetition) [score 2]

Quick regression timeline:
- 2024-11-09: rollout started for routing fallback (canary)
- 2024-11-10: rollout to 50% traffic, small kernel change applied to runtime (kfetch v0.9.2)
- 2024-11-11 03:00 (UTC): observed first drift in synthetic smoke tests (not flagged)
- 2024-11-12 23:10: manual sampling run (this doc)

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) KV-cache interaction + new fallback introduces occasional incomplete KV reads -> truncated output. (high)
B) Kernel change (kfetch v0.9.2) has a race on stream flush for mid-sequence termination. (med-high)
C) Input pre-processing edge-case: certain multi-line prompts trigger off-by-one tokenization bug. (medium)
D) Downstream trimming in routing layer (truncate on newline) mis-applied for some model variants. (low)

Quick experiments to run (fast, non-prod):
- Re-run same seed against pre-rollout cluster snapshot (2024-11-08 image) and count >=2 scores. (priority)
- Force-disable KV cache on 3 hosts and resample n=100. Compare truncation rate. (priority)
- A/B: rollback kfetch to v0.9.1 for small window and monitor. (if rollback easy)
- Add verbose logging for kv read lengths when response length < expected. (requires infra)

Instrument suggestions (observability):
- Add histogram metric: response_end_reason (normal|eos|truncated|error).
- Emit kv-cache read success ratio per-request-id.
- Sample full token stream for truncated cases and persist to s3/gcs for offline debug.

Immediate actions I took:
- Opened quick ticket GH: redwood/inference#1847 (linked). Left initial triage notes.
- Pinged Samir in #eng-applied-ml with short snippet and sample ids.
- Tagged a small subset of examples and uploaded to /tmp/eval-clusters/midnight-run for follow-up.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Pattern looks more like state leak / cache read than model weights corruption. Repetition frequently contains same short phrase which smells like partial re-use of previously returned tokens.
- If this is KV mis-read, disabling KV should drop token savings but fix truncation; good diagnostic.
- Need to keep experiments small and reproducible; attach seeds + timestamps.

Next steps (tomorrow):
- Run non-prod replay against 2024-11-08 images and kfetch=v0.9.1. Collect metrics.
- If repro, prepare short blameline for SRE to schedule rollback window.
- Draft short customer-facing note if we see increased incidence on hosted.

Open questions:
- Are there any other rollouts at same time (infra autoscaler bump?) — check release-engineering log.
- Any correlation with model size/quantization? The samples were all from mid-sized LLMs (13B quant).

Scratchpad / raw markers (copy of sample ids):
- s-20241112-001, s-20241112-007, s-20241112-019, s-20241112-021, s-20241112-027

End.
